New agricultural or NRM practices
• Pit planting. One gets more crop yields from this method because you plant more seeds in a small area. It retains moisture and reduces soil erosion.
• Conservation agriculture including the use of herbicides and not making ridges.
• When we lay the crop residue we wait for the rains to come and when they come moisture is retained.
• It also adds to soil fertility.
• It protects the soil from erosion.
• For the elderly this method has helped them because it eases the workload.
• Rearing of hybrid goats.
• This was brought by XX and some agricultural organizations. The goats are larger and fetch a good price
• Agro-forestry/ afforestation.
• The idea is to retain soil fertility.
• The idea is to protect the environment and the soil
• Bee keeping which helps to make money.
• The use of elevated goat houses.
• Goats are not attacked by disease because the urine trickles to the ground and parasites remain on the ground. It also protects goats from predators like hyenas.
• Clay stoves for cooking (locally known as Chitetezo mbaula). These use less firewood and retain heat for a long time.

In the past the soil was still fertile and cotton performed well in the fields but now the soil has lost fertility and conservation agriculture has come in where people are planting groundnuts and maize.
Cotton prices went down which de-motivated people from growing it.

In the past people engaged in cotton farming because it was an important commercial product. Now, people have seen some changes for instance goats are performing better on the market. Nowadays when someone plants groundnuts and when they plant cotton they can notice the difference in terms of how much they make.
When it comes to maize, in the past people planted the local varieties which did not perform well but now people plant hybrid varieties like DKC and Fumba that perform well.
Men and women usually follow the same customs unless there are some disputes in the household.

There are some customs and roles that are drawn along gender lines. Men are more active in tobacco farming because women say “they do not eat tobacco”. Women usually go for subsistence crops like maize and groundnuts because they are the ones that look after the kids and food is a priority.
Most women refuse to apply herbicides and pesticides.
